ADMINISTRATIVE_PROCESSES.definition: Generation of data during healthcare system operations, e.g. appointments, coding, payments.

ADMISSION_DISCHARGE.definition: Process of hospitalizing, treating, and releasing a patient, generating clinical and administrative data.

AUTOMATIC_GENERATION.definition: Data passively collected by sensors, apps, or devices without active input from users.

BIOBANK_COLLECTION.definition: Acquisition and storage of biological samples from individuals for current or future research.

CENSUS_DATA.definition: Large-scale demographic and socio-economic data collection conducted by public authorities.

CLINICAL_TRIAL.definition: Structured, controlled investigation into medical treatments, interventions or technologies.

COHORT.definition: Longitudinal tracking of a defined group over time to observe health outcomes.

DISEASE_MONITORING.definition: Surveillance and reporting of disease outbreaks and infections.

EHEALTH_APPLICATION.definition: Data created through interaction with digital health apps by individuals.

GEOSPATIAL_MONITORING.definition: Data collection using satellite or location-based systems to monitor environmental or health exposures.

HEALTHCARE_VISIT.definition: Patient interaction with a healthcare professional for diagnosis, treatment, or consultation.

HEALTH_REGISTRIES.definition: Government-led databases tracking diseases, treatments, or health trends at national level.

HEALTH_SURVEILLANCE.definition: Systematic collection and analysis of health data to inform public health action.

HEALTH_SURVEY.definition: Collection of structured self-reported data about health behaviours, symptoms, and determinants.

HOSPITAL_RECORDS.definition: Institutional system aggregating clinical and operational hospital data.

INSURANCE_CLAIMS.definition: Data generated through processing health-related financial transactions and coverage validation.

LABORATORY_TESTS.definition: Data produced by clinical or diagnostic testing in a lab setting.

MEASUREMENTS.definition: Collection of physiological, anthropometric, or other health indicators (e.g., blood pressure, BMI).

MEDICAL_DEVICES.definition: Clinical or home use of health technologies that generate or record data during patient care.

MEDICAL_REGISTRY.definition: Structured, ongoing data collection on a specific disease, procedure, or treatment population.

MODELS_SIMULATIONS.definition: Use of computational or statistical models to simulate clinical or population outcomes.

MUNICIPAL_REPOSITORY.definition: Centralised local government data collection on public health and services.

NONMEDICAL_APPLICATION.definition: Data collected through platforms or tools not designed for medical use (e.g., fitness apps).

OBSERVATIONAL_DATA.definition: Data generated by non-interventional observation of patients or populations.

PATIENT_OUTCOMES.definition: Self-reported data provided by patients on their health status and quality of life.

PRESCRIBING_DISPENSING.definition: Issuing or providing medication to patients by healthcare professionals or pharmacies.

PROBABILITY_SURVEY.definition: Data collected through a statistically representative sampling process.

QUALITY_REGISTRIES.definition: Nationally coordinated registries collecting data on treatment quality, outcomes, and standards.

QUALITY_REGISTRY.definition: Collection of healthcare quality indicators to monitor care delivery and outcomes.

RESEARCH_DATABASE.definition: Purpose-built repository developed as part of a research activity for future reuse.

RESEARCH_PROJECT.definition: Targeted scientific activity to answer specific health-related research questions.

ROUTINE_RECORDS.definition: Administrative or system-generated records not primarily intended for health, but used secondarily.

SAMPLE_COLLECTIONS.definition: Systematic gathering of human material (e.g. blood, DNA) for storage and analysis.

SURVEILLANCE.definition: Ongoing, systematic monitoring of public or population health indicators.
